spec: PLAN.md 3.39.13 (V2Q clone mode), compact rules of 3.39.12; implemented in src/secutg/v2/join/
notes: V2Q:<code>:<nonce_b64url>:<ct_b64url>. <code> is exactly 32 characters of 0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ (upper case, no separators, no I/L/O/U leniency); <nonce> is 24 bytes; <ct> at least the 16-byte tag. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

key = BLAKE2b-256("tg-v2-join-v1" || base32decode(code)); XChaCha20-Poly1305-IETF; AAD = "secutg/v2clone/v1" (constant). The retired add_device format used AAD "secutg/v2join/v1"; a reader tries that AAD only when the new one fails, to answer old_version instead of undecryptable.

plaintext is JSON with EXACTLY these keys in EXACTLY this order and no whitespace: v(=2), kind(="v2clone"), peer_user_id(non-empty string), binding_id(32B), epoch(number >= 1), safety_code(string), roster[[identity_pk, encapsulation_pk], ...] (2-element string arrays, ascending device_id, at least 2), masters[m_e, m_(e-1), ...] (base64url 32B; masters[i] is generation epoch-i; 1..epoch entries), own{identity_seed(32B), encapsulation_sk(32B)}, expires_ms(number >= 0). Any other key, order, or type is malformed.

own = the showing device's keys FOR THIS BINDING (its per-binding identity if it has one, else its global identity). Derived on the reader: identity_pk / 64-byte sk = crypto_sign_seed_keypair(identity_seed); encapsulation_pk = crypto_scalarmult_base(encapsulation_sk); device_id = base64url(sha256(identity_pk)). Roster device ids MUST be strictly ascending; own.device_id MUST be in the roster; and (Web's addition, resolving the spec) own.encapsulation_pk MUST equal that roster entry's encapsulation_pk — else malformed.

Errors, the FIRST failing check wins: malformed (text syntax); old_version (AEAD opens only under the legacy AAD, or the plaintext is an object with v == 1 or kind == "v2join"); undecryptable (AEAD opens under neither AAD); malformed (payload / derivation); expired (now_ms > expires_ms + 120000); wrong_chat (peer_user_id != the chat scanned in); already_paired (has_current_binding, or the binding_id is tombstoned on the scanner).

Install: binding {chat_id = the chat scanned in, binding_id, epoch, device_roster = roster device ids, device_keys from roster, txn_id = "clone:" + binding_id, own_identity = own (derived), safety_code as carried, verified = false}; masters[0] current, the rest historical. Immediately sendable; nothing is sent.

Capacity: QR byte mode. ECC M holds 2331 bytes, ECC L 2953. History wins over the error correction level: for k = 0, 1, 2, ... OLDEST history masters dropped, if the text fits M use M, else if it fits L use L, else drop one more; only when the current master alone exceeds L is the code too large. Measured: a 2-device roster with the current master alone is 841 bytes; each history master adds 61 bytes; each roster device adds 125. The fit cases pin the exact numbers; rule-* cases pin the decision at synthetic limits (max_bytes_override).

Actors: ed25519 keys from crypto_sign_seed_keypair(seed); x25519 pk = scalarmult_base(sk); master of epoch e = byte(0x40+e)*32; rosters are taken in the order o, p, o2, p2, o3, p3, o4, p4. now_ms / chat_id / has_current_binding are the fixed ones unless a case sets its own.
